title: Tensor compatibility of the normalized proper/open interchange
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-fix-six-functor-datum], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, $R=\mathcal O_E$ and $A_n=R/\varpi_E^n$. Let
$$\begin{array}{ccc}U&\xrightarrow{k_1}&V\\ r\downarrow&&\downarrow p\\ W&\xrightarrow{i}&Z\end{array}$$
be a commutative square of finite-type $k$-schemes, with $p,r$ proper and $i,k_1$ open immersions [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. No Cartesian hypothesis is imposed. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The coefficient setting is either (a) ordinary unbounded derived categories of constant $A_n$-module sheaves, for a fixed $n\ge1$, or (b) $D(\mathscr S_T)$, where $\mathscr S_T$ is the category of strict semilinear systems of $(A_n)_T$-module sheaves of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. In (b) use the simultaneous system operations and adjunctions in that node; in (a) use the ordinary derived operations of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Write $P_u$ for pullback, $S_u$ for derived direct image, and $J_j$ for exact open extension, with $P_u\dashv S_u$ and $J_j\dashv P_j$. Tensor means derived tensor in the specified coefficient category. The comparisons $P_u(M\otimes N)\cong P_uM\otimes P_uN$ and pullback composition are the canonical ones [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback].

For $M$ on the source of $u$ and $N$ on its target, define $\pi_{u;M,N}:S_uM\otimes N\to S_u(M\otimes P_uN)$ as the $P_u\dashv S_u$-adjunct of $(\varepsilon_{u,M}\otimes1)\mu_u$. Let $\gamma_{j;M,N}:J_jM\otimes N\xrightarrow{\sim}J_j(M\otimes P_jN)$ be the unit-normalized open tensor comparison of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Let $V_W=V\times_ZW$ with projections $b:V_W\to V$, $q:V_W\to W$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and let $s=(k_1,r):U\to V_W$; it is an open-and-closed immersion. Normalize
$$\lambda:P_iS_pJ_{k_1}\xrightarrow{\sim}S_r$$
by open restriction $P_iS_p\cong S_qP_b$, $P_bJ_{k_1}\cong J_s$, the open-and-closed identification $J_s\cong S_s$ and the direct-image compositor $S_qS_s\cong S_r$. Define $\Gamma:J_iS_r\to S_pJ_{k_1}$ to be the $J_i\dashv P_i$-adjunct of $\lambda^{-1}$, using the identity normalization $P_iJ_i\cong1$. This is the normalized finite proper/open map, or the actual derived-system map with this normalization of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]; no invertibility of $\Gamma$ is assumed.

For every object $M$ on $U$ and $N$ on $Z$ in the chosen unbounded categories, the following two maps from $J_iS_rM\otimes N$ to $S_pJ_{k_1}(M\otimes P_{k_1}P_pN)$ agree:
$$S_p(\gamma_{k_1;M,P_pN})\,\pi_{p;J_{k_1}M,N}\,(\Gamma_M\otimes1_N)
=\Gamma_{M\otimes P_rP_iN}\,J_i(\pi_{r;M,P_iN})\,\gamma_{i;S_rM,N}.$$
On the right insert the canonical identification $P_rP_iN\cong P_{k_1}P_pN$ coming from $ir=pk_1$. Juxtaposition composes right to left. In setting (b) the equality holds in the derived category of systems itself, before evaluation, restriction of scalars or total inverse limit. No constructibility, Tor-amplitude, normalization or etale-origin condition on $M,N$ is required, and no invertibility of either projection morphism is asserted.

source.place: Compactification-independence sentence: compatibility of refinement comparisons with counits and j_!; expanded through the normalized proper/open interchange, using the open restriction argument of the following paragraph.

proof.text: The open immersions $i,k_1$ are quasi-compact, as required by the existing proper/open projection-mate lemma. Indeed $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian (a field has only the ideals $0,k$), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $V,Z$ Noetherian. For every affine open $H$ of either target, the inverse image under the respective open immersion is an open subscheme of that Noetherian target. It is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. This is exactly quasi-compactness of the open immersion. The other geometric hypotheses, commutativity and properness of $p,r$, are already assumed.

proof.text:
In case (a), write $\alpha:P_pJ_i\to J_{k_1}P_r$ and $g:J_iS_r\to S_pJ_{k_1}$ for the clopen map and its proper mate in [lem-sf-proper-open-projection-mate]. Its transpose is $J_{k_1}\varepsilon_r\circ\alpha S_r$ by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Apply [lem-sf-cartesian-open-adjunction-restriction] to $(p,i)$ and set $H=S_rM$. Under $P_iJ_i=1$, $P_bJ_{k_1}=J_s$ and $P_b\beta=1$, its unit equation and naturality of $E$ identify $\lambda_M P_i(g_M)$ with
$$H\xrightarrow{\eta_q}S_qP_qH\xrightarrow{S_q\pi_s}S_qJ_sP_sP_qH\xrightarrow{S_qJ_s\varepsilon_r}S_qJ_sM\xrightarrow{a_M}S_rM.$$
Here the identity restriction of $\beta$ is [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], and $a$ uses exactly the clopen identification and direct-image compositor in $\lambda$.

proof.text: [lem-sf-clopen-composite-counit-normalization], applied with $X=V_W$, $q:V_W\to W$ and the stipulated clopen $s:U\to V_W$, makes the displayed composite $1_{S_rM}$. Thus $P_i(g_M)=\lambda_M^{-1}$. The defining $J_i\dashv P_i$ adjunct of $\Gamma_M$ is also $\lambda_M^{-1}$, so the adjunction bijection gives $g_M=\Gamma_M$. This only compares two transposes; it does not assume that $g$ or $\Gamma$ is invertible.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-proper-open-projection-mate] with $(A,B,C,D,k)=(U,V,W,Z,k_1)$. In (a), $\Lambda=A_n$ is finite commutative; Step 1 checks quasi-compactness and Steps 2--3 identify its proper mate with $\Gamma$. Its $\pi_h$ is our counit-defined $\pi_h$, and its $\delta_j$ is our $\gamma_j$, with precisely [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Its equation with sides exchanged is the required equation, inserting $P_rP_i\cong P_{k_1}P_p$ from $ir=pk_1$. In (b), its final statement already gives this equation with the intrinsically normalized system $\Gamma_Q$. [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] supplies the simultaneous system operations, so this is an equality in $D(\mathscr S)$ before evaluation. No projection map is inverted and no input bounds or extra hypotheses are introduced.

lean.statement:
theorem properOpenProjectionMate
    (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ]
    {A B C D : Scheme.{u}} (k : A ⟶ B) (r : A ⟶ C)
    (p : B ⟶ D) (i : C ⟶ D) [IsOpenImmersion k] [IsOpenImmersion i]
    [QuasiCompact k] [QuasiCompact i] [IsProper r] [IsProper p]
    (h : k ≫ p = r ≫ i)
    (M : ProperOpenDerived Λ A) (N : ProperOpenDerived Λ D) :
    (properOpenTensorIso Λ i ((ProperOpenPush Λ r).obj M) N).hom ≫
      (ProperOpenShriek Λ i).map (properOpenProjection Λ r M ((ProperOpenPull Λ i).obj N)) ≫
      (ProperOpenShriek Λ i).map ((ProperOpenPush Λ r).map
        (((ProperOpenTensor Λ A).obj M).map
          ((properOpenPullSquareIso Λ k r p i h).hom.app N))) ≫
      (properOpenMate Λ k r p i h).app
        (((ProperOpenTensor Λ A).obj M).obj
          ((ProperOpenPull Λ k).obj ((ProperOpenPull Λ p).obj N))) =
    properOpenMateTensorMap Λ k r p i h M N ≫
      properOpenProjection Λ p ((ProperOpenShriek Λ k).obj M) N ≫
      (ProperOpenPush Λ p).map
        (properOpenTensorIso Λ k M ((ProperOpenPull Λ p).obj N)).hom
